method.cpu: Cumulative Windows job kernel and user time includes exited desktop descendants; divided by wall time, normalized to one logical CPU.
method.working_set: Sum of process working sets, counting shared resident pages in each process.
method.foreground: Native foreground PID sampled with counters; every sample must match the desktop for foreground qualification.
method.observation: CDP client detached throughout each counter interval; debugging listener remained enabled. No verbose browser logging, axe, or screen reader during these intervals.
repeat_adaptations: Reused the earlier isolated test profile.
Waited for explicit user foreground confirmation before the settling period.
method.settings: Windows settings and DNS configuration unchanged; the service was not installed.

scope: The first interval ran while the PR13 harness was being developed. It is diagnostic evidence.
The repeated interval reached the foreground initially but did not retain it for every sample.
Both observed CPU averages exceed 0.5 percent of one logical CPU. Formal complete-process acceptance remains unassessed.
Foreground conditions differ, so the two intervals are reported separately.
A separate instrumented trace identified short-lived WebView unzip.mojom.Unzipper utilities. That trace is not a budget measurement and does not establish the cause of all CPU usage.
This 20-logical-CPU, 32-GiB development host is not the four-logical-CPU, 8-GiB reference machine.
The new service startup logging feature was not installed on this host during these measurements.
result: CPU accounting now includes exited desktop descendants. Foreground and simultaneous service/desktop resource qualification remain open.
